subject.title: [Feature]: Memory/Context Improvements (metrics + global semantic search + conversation chaining + preload on restart)

question: Should OpenClaw define core-supported surfaces for agent-facing metrics, cross-session semantic recall, normal-session handoff, and restart preload, or keep some of these as experimental/plugin-owned capabilities?
rationale: The code can support pieces of the request, but the remaining behavior sets API shape, defaults, transcript/docs visibility, auth/cost attribution, and gateway lifecycle policy that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Split Into Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and split the remaining metrics, memory search scope, session continuation, and restart-preload decisions into narrow product/security issues before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Issues
options.body: Let the open narrower issues carry their slices while this issue stays tracking-only until the overlaps converge.

options.title: Close After Replacement Issues
options.body: Close this only after maintainers create or nominate canonical narrower issues for every remaining API, default, and security decision.

recommendation.title: Split Into Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and split the remaining metrics, memory search scope, session continuation, and restart-preload decisions into narrow product/security issues before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the prior keep-open review and has the strongest recent history across the central memory, usage, and docs surfaces.
